name: Marina Bay Street Circuit

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap circuit relation 421263 (ways ordered by shared nodes, © OSM contributors), station 0 at its "finish" node 13826310653 (the "start" node 4281759834 is 138 m further on); 2023+ layout (Turns 16-19 under the grandstand replaced by a straight)
sources.width: Published / typical: ~12 m street circuit, wider pit straight (15 m) and Raffles Boulevard (13.5 m), narrow Anderson Bridge (~10.5 m), Esplanade 12.5 m; no free government orthophoto for Singapore
sources.elevation: Copernicus GLO-30 DSM (tile N01 E103), ground estimate = 15th percentile of centre/edge samples within +-150 m (buildings, trees and bridges only raise a surface model), then ~100 m moving averages; result 3-9 m, consistent with a nearly flat reclaimed-land circuit
sources.pit: OpenStreetMap way 100484287 (Pit Lane, member of relation 421263)
sources.trim: Maximum downforce street circuit (like Monaco/Hungary), many 90-degree corners
sources.pitLimit: FIA Singapore GP event notes: pit lane speed limit 60 km/h (long pit lane)
sources.pitLoss: Typical F1 pit-stop loss ~28 s at Singapore, one of the highest of the season (F1/Pirelli strategy previews); approximate
sources.raceLaps: FIA 2026 Singapore GP: 62 laps; 2026 sprint weekend, sprint run over 20 laps (results, 11 Oct 2026)

notes: Anticlockwise. 19-turn 2023+ numbering assigned from curvature peaks; numbering of the Raffles Boulevard kinks (T5/T6) and the final sector (T15-T19) is approximate. Timing line = OSM finish node; the start line is ~140 m further. Pit limit: F1 used 60 km/h at Singapore in recent years (verify per event).
